title: Gangsters ran the clubs and treated musicians well
summary: Smith says local White racketeers ran the clubs and were the musician's best friend.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Tell me. Talking about the Kansas City club scene, was that run by gangsters?
What were they? Local guys or Mafia?
They was mostly the local fellows.
And what kind of rackets were they into?
Mmm, all I knew was just racketeering. They had a hand in all the liquor stores and a hand in all the cleaning-pressing shops, and then all the cement mixing outfit...
How did they treat the musicians?
Yeah. The gangster was the musician's best

Yeah. From the Cotton Club on down, all of them, I don't care what anybody says, I tell them that all the time. Those were the fellows that were taking care of the musicians, them gangsters running them clubs. The Grand Terrace and all them, them gangsters run it. All you do is just go and do your work and tend your business.
